subject: Throughput threshold SLA variance request
messages:
From: Adam Lyons <adam@clearcure.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Throughput threshold SLA variance request

Hi Neha,

We're ramping up for our Feb 17 feature rollout and are seeing a short, predictable spike in inference traffic tied to our nightly batch + early-morning consumer queries. Over the last two days our 95th-percentile token throughput has briefly exceeded the rate tier in our contract and we started to see throttling around 05:30 PST this morning. Latency rose from ~80ms to ~320ms for affected calls and a small percentage of requests hit a 429.

We expect a controlled window of elevated load between Feb 16 03:00 - 07:00 PST and Feb 17 04:00 - 09:00 PST (approx. additional 1.2M tokens/hour). Can Redwood temporarily lift our rate cap or apply a one-week throughput variance so we don't hit fairness throttles during this go-live? We're prepared to share traffic snapshots and to accept tighter monitoring/alerts.

We're trying to avoid engineering workarounds that slow the rollout. Please let us know what information you need, any limits on exceptions, and an estimate of how quickly this could be enabled.

Thanks,
Adam
Adam Lyons
Director, Platform Engineering
ClearCure Health
[Attachment: traffic_snapshot_02122026.csv]
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Adam Lyons <adam@clearcure.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput threshold SLA variance request

Hi Adam — thanks for the heads up and for the snapshot. I copied Vivek to weigh in on operational options, and Marissa for any commercial/credits conversations. A few quick Qs to help us scope the request:

- Can you confirm the exact 1-hour windows (start/end) in UTC?
- Is the traffic spike bursty (short sub-minute bursts) or sustained at elevated RPS?
- Are all calls routed to a single model endpoint / route? If you have per-route breakdowns please attach.

Operationally we have two paths: a temporary rate-tier uplift (policy exception to allow higher token throughput) or a short-lived Dedicated burst allocation if you need guaranteed capacity and lower tail latency. The first is faster but subject to fairness policing; the second gives stronger latency guarantees but requires provisioning.

If you grant us permission to enable enhanced monitoring (additional metrics + a short retention of high-granularity traces) we can open the window quickly and add an automatic rollback if error/latency thresholds are exceeded.

I can do a quick call with Vivek and your SREs today if helpful.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Adam Lyons <adam@clearcure.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput threshold SLA variance request

Adam / Neha — quick technical read: thanks for the snapshot, that helps. A few notes and a proposed plan: 

1) From the traces the pattern looks like a sustained elevated RPS during the early-morning windows, not microbursts. That favors a short Dedicated burst vs a transient rate-cap bump.

2) If you can enable our prefix KV caching (small client change) you'll shave a lot of repeated prefix tokens off. We'll provide a config snippet.

3) Proposed immediate action (48–72h turnaround):
   - Apply a temporary rate-tier variance (increase token threshold by 45%) for the two concrete windows you provide.
   - Enable high-granularity tracing for those windows and set automatic rollback triggers (5xx > 1.5% OR p95 latency > 250ms OR sustained 429s).
   - If p95 latency does not drop under 200ms within first two hours of the window, escalate to a Dedicated-backed fallback route.

4) Monitoring: we will create a dedicated dashboard and an automated PagerDuty hook for Redwood SRE + your on-call.

Marissa — if we do the variance, can we offer a partial credit if the variance leads to noticeable customer impact (we should flag this in the variance doc)?

Vivek
VP, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Adam Lyons <adam@clearcure.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearcure.com
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput threshold SLA variance request

Thanks Vivek — validated. Windows below (UTC attached as well):
- 2026-02-17 11:00–15:00 UTC (primary consumer surge)
- 2026-02-18 12:00–17:00 UTC (post-release catch-up)

Traffic shape: sustained elevated RPS (~+35% baseline) across the two windows, not sub-minute spikes. Per-route: 86% of traffic to /v1/generate/curie-like-model, remainder to embeddings route.

We approve Redwood enabling high-granularity tracing and the rollback triggers you listed. We would prefer the Dedicated fallback if latency remains high — availability is critical for our users.

I've uploaded a slightly edited draft SLA variance form here: https://app.redwood.example/documents/RDW-4571/sla-variance-draft and DocuSign link for procurement: https://www.docusign.com/clearcure-sla-waiver-4272.

Attaching the final traffic CSV.

Adam
[Attachment: traffic_snapshot_02122026.csv]
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Adam Lyons <adam@clearcure.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput threshold SLA variance request — confirmed window and controls

Adam — thanks, all set. Summary of what Redwood will do (agreed scope):

- Window: 2026-02-16 00:00 PST through 2026-02-22 23:59 PST (we widened by a day on either side to cover rollout variability per your team ask).
- Policy change: temporary rate-tier uplift of +45% tokens for endpoints: /v1/generate/curie-like-model and /v1/embeddings.
- Fallback: automatic routing to a small Dedicated pool if p95 latency > 200ms after the first 2 hours of elevated load.
- Rollback triggers: 5xx > 1.5%, sustained 429s > 0.5% or p95 > 400ms. If any trigger fires we will revert the variance and notify both teams.
- Monitoring: we will provision a dashboard and a PagerDuty integration; Redwood SRE will monitor first two windows in real time.
- Commercials: Marissa will follow up on a one-week service credit if the variance leads to material user impact.

Next steps for ClearCure: sign the variance DocuSign link (procurement) and confirm your on-call person for the PagerDuty integration. We will not enable the Dedicated fallback without explicit customer approval to absorb the additional Dedicated cost.

I'll attach the signed variance form to the ticket once signed.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-sla-variance-draft.docx]
